Verify that, if batteries are employed for SOF backup power, adequate charging methods and checks are provided and installation provisions for all batteries are safe.

versions.text: Criterion: Verify that, if batteries are employed for backup power, adequate charging methods and monitoring are provided and installation provisions for all batteries are safe. Standard: Minimum of 30 minutes capability is provided where backup batteries are used. Nickel-Cadmium batteries are prohibited. Location of lead acid batteries in the same bay as flight critical components is prohibited. Adequate charging methods exist and monitoring is performed to assess battery health, and condition status is provided to the crew. If dedicated batteries are used for the VCF, use of these batteries is exclusive to the VCF. Method of Compliance: Verification methods include analysis, tests, simulation and review of documentation. Analyses confirm the battery architecture and loads. Assumptions are validated via simulation and testing in representative environments. Hardware in the Loop (HITL) and ground tests confirm battery life, loads and health. The most adverse electrical loading, environmental, fault, and endurance conditions required of the VCF are tested. Battery integrity is verified by pre/post flight checklists, maintenance tech data, analyses and ground testing. References: JSSG-2008: 3.0, 3.1, 3.1.2, 3.1.5.2, 3.1.7.2, 3.1.11.11.2, 3.1.13, 3.2.2.2.2, 3.2.2.2.5, associated section 4 paragraphs. 14 CFR 23.1351-23.1367, 25.1351-25.1363, 23.141-23.253, 25.21-25.255, 23.321-23.459, 25.321-25.459, 23.1501-23.1529, 25.1501-25.1529.

Standard: Where batteries are employed as backup power source to VCF, they provide sufficient capacity for VCF not to degrade below Operational State IV. If batteries are used for transient suppression, they provide suppression capability for VCF not to degrade below Operational State II. Battery health is monitored and status provided to the flight crew. Batteries that are exclusive to VCF operation are not to be shared with other subsystems. Method of Compliance: Prior to entering flight test, verify the standard by the following method(s): Examination.
(1) Review VCF and EPS ICD for use of batteries.
(2) Review EPS architecture with respect to battery integration. Identify functions which are retained and those which are shed when batteries are used as backup power. Analysis.
  (1) Complete an ELA and verify proper coverage of electrical loads when using batteries for backup power. Test.
    (1) Lab test: Conduct FMET of the EPS to verify redundancy management including adequacy of battery usage coverage.
    (2) Lab test: Conduct HITL simulation to verify no worse than VCF Operational State IV while on battery power only.
    (3) Lab test: Conduct HITL simulation to verify battery suppression capability meets no worse than VCF Operational State II.
